If we go through the year-on-year Q1 FY27 performance, revenue grew by 61.5% to INR166.6 crores.
Cash and cash equivalents were INR133.75 crores compared with INR163 crores at the year-end of FY26.
Growth & demand: I'm glad to share that we have started the year on the strong note delivering our strong quarterly performance revenue of INR116 crores, a year -on-year growth of 61.5% along with the PAT has grown significantly on the year -on-year basis to a INR29.7 crores.
If we go through for the quarter-on-quarter basis performance, our revenue increased by 12.1% to INR166.6 crores.
Our strong order book as on July 31st was about INR3,000 crores.

So, it is not a segment-specific, but of course, sometimes in a some product we may have a some 2%, 3%, 4% lesser margin, and some product have a little bit more margin.
So, margin will be a similar in the range of 30% and above, something like that.
Capex & expansion: We operate three manufacturing facilities with an aggregated area of around 80,000 square meters with an annualized installed machine capacity of 3.2 million hours as on 30th June.

In addition, the annualized machining capacity has increased by approximately 20.7% compared by FY26, providing additional headroom for the execution of the existing order book and the future programs in which we are working on.
So, at present, as of first quarter 30th June 2026, our annualized capacity for all the three plants is 31 lakhs, around 32 lakhs.
Balance sheet & cash: Overall, the improvement in net working capital was primarily driven by normalization of the inventory and receivables, partially offset by the reduction in payable days.
So, in the working capital, you can just we are seeing in terms of -- in this range, and we are we are working on to improve another 10% to 20% in the range of to improve the working capital.
So, from the IPO proceeds, we have paid debt of INR50 crores, that is a long -term debt, and at present, we have a total debt of INR390 crores.

Guidance & outlook: Net debt-to-equity improved to 0.34x in FY26 from 1.6x in FY25, reflects strong cash generations and prudent capital management.
It has grown from INR 57 crores in FY23 to INR 83 crores in FY24, to INR 283 crores in FY25, and now to around INR 3,000 crores as of May 25 , 2026 .

So, just to understand how should we think of the ramp up, you have announced a INR 900 crore NPA, how should we think of the ramp up from FY27, FY28, if you can guide on some numbers that will be helpful.
Growth & demand: The order book, as on 25th May 2026, more than INR 3,000 crores of order book has been indicated, and a strong order book flow is going on.
The order book mix is currently led by Energy at 74%, followed by Motion and Automation at 14%, and Industrial Equipment is standing at around 12%.
Our order book stands today at around INR 3,000 crores plus, and we operate from manufacturing facilities with an annualized capacity of 26 lakhs hours and growin g steadily.
Margins & costs: Profit after tax increased to 80.9% to INR 79.3 crores with a PAT margin improved to 15.5% from 12.8% last year.
PAT rose 43.4% to INR 29.3 crores with margin holding steady at 19.7%.
And in Q4, we saw a sharp gross margin compression, about 450 basis points against the last two qu arters.
Capex & expansion: So, in case we have been able to grow our capacity year-on-year, let's say by 40 % or 50%.

This reflects our conscious efforts to strengthen the balance sheet and reduce leverage risk.

Going forward, we remain focused on optimizing working capital by the end of this financial year through three specific levers: ➢ Inventory rationalizations. ➢ Normalizations of receivable cycles. ➢ Continued payable optimizations through disciplined executions and operational planning.

Guidance & outlook: Our performance during this period reflects strong revenue acceleration by 80% over the Quarter 3 FY25.
Meaningful expansion in profitability with a EB ITDA higher than 110% from Quarter 3 FY25.
For the performance of Quarter 3 FY26, with a performance compared to the Quarter 3 of Financial ‘25, our revenue from operations stood at INR134.4 crores, registering a year-on-year growth of 81.6%.
Growth & demand: Continued growth in our order book up to a INR2,900 crores.
EBITDA for the quarter was INR51.2 crores, reflecting a growth of 112.4% year-on-year.
In FY25, we were at INR283 crores and as of March 11th, 2026 our order book stands at approximately INR2910 crores, reflecting a strong order inflow and a long -term customer commitment.
Margins & costs: If we see the EBITDA margin improved to 33.4% from 31.7%.
And adding to the Bhavin's point, overall in our cost structure, materials contributes less than 30% of the total cost average.
So in terms of average COGS is, you know, raw material material margin is a 30% average of the product line.
Capex & expansion: So if you see our presentation, so we have added in the present plant also we have increased our capacity is around 40% to 50% as compared to FY '25.
So, the increase in capacity in in existing plant is to the extent of 40% to 50%.
And so, adding to that, in our IPO prospectus, there are also some of investment we have given into our existing plant, which will or add another some capacity in our existing plant.
Balance sheet & cash: The improvement reflects operating leverage benefits, better product mix and disciplined cost management.
If we see the 6 months financial year ‘26 net debt -to-equity, which remains stable to 1.7 times improving significantly from 2.9 times in FY24.
For 6 mont hs financial year ‘26 our net working capital cycle stood to 256 days compared to 283 days in the financial ‘25, reflecting a clear improvement in our working capital management.
Risks & challenges: So basically there is no as such raw material risk as far as the material is concerned.
And now they have to mitigate the risk of the concentrated supplier.
So we will be in the growth trajectory, but the world is overall in the uncertain market.
